readings.title: Absalom's Conspiracy
readings.subtitle: Stealing the Hearts of Israel
readings.text: [2 Samuel 15:1] And it came to be after this that Aḇshalom provided himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him. [2] And Aḇshalom used to rise early and stand beside the way to the gate. And so it was, whenever anyone who had a lawsuit came to the sovereign for a right-ruling, that Aḇshalom would call to him and say, “What city are you from?” And he would say, “Your servant is from such and such a tribe of Yisra’ĕl.” [3] And Aḇshalom would say to him, “See, your matters are good and right, but there is no deputy of the sovereign to hear you.” [4] And Aḇshalom would say, “Oh, that I were made judge in the land, and everyone who has a lawsuit or cause would come to me, and I would give him right-ruling.” [5] And it came to be, whenever anyone came near to bow down to him, that he would put out <dn>את</dn> his hand and take him and kiss him. [6] And Aḇshalom did this to all Yisra’ĕl who came to the sovereign for right-ruling. Thus Aḇshalom stole <dn>את</dn> the hearts of the men of Yisra’ĕl. [7] And it came to be after forty years that Aḇshalom said to the sovereign, “Please, let me go to Ḥeḇron and pay <dn>את</dn> my vow which I vowed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [8] “For your servant took a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall indeed bring me back to Yerushalayim, then I shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ” [9] And the sovereign said to him, “Go in peace.” So he arose and went to Ḥeḇron. [10] But Aḇshalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the ram’s horn, then you shall say, ‘Aḇshalom is sovereign in Ḥeḇron!’ ” [11] And two hundred men from Yerushalayim went with Aḇshalom, who were invited and went in their innocence, and they did not know a matter. [12] And Aḇshalom sent for <dn>את</dn> Aḥithophel the Gilonite, Dawiḏ’s counsellor, from his city, from Giloh, while he offered <dn>את</dn> slaughterings. And the conspiracy grew strong, for the people with Aḇshalom continually increased.

readings.title: The Flight of Dawiḏ
readings.subtitle: Leaving Jerusalem Behind
readings.text: [2 Samuel 15:13] And a messenger came to Dawiḏ, saying, “The hearts of the men of Yisra’ĕl are after Aḇshalom.” [14] So Dawiḏ said to all his servants who were with him at Yerushalayim, “Rise up, and let us flee, or else we shall have no escape from Aḇshalom. Hasten to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly and bring evil upon us, and smite <dn>את</dn> the city with the edge of the sword.” [15] And the sovereign’s servants said to the sovereign, “Look, your servants are ready to do whatever my master the sovereign chooses.” [16] And the sovereign went out with all his household after him. But the sovereign left <dn>את</dn> ten women, concubines, to guard the house. [17] And the sovereign went out with all the people after him, and stopped at the outskirts. [18] And all his servants passed before him, and all the Kerĕthites and all the Pelĕthites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had followed him from Gath, passed before the sovereign. [19] And the sovereign said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why are you also going with us? Go back and remain with the sovereign. For you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place. [20] “In fact, you came only yesterday. Should I make you wander up and down with us today, since I go I know not where? Return, and take <dn>את</dn> your brothers back. Kindness and truth be with you.” [21] And Ittai answered the sovereign and said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, and as my master the sovereign lives, surely in whatever place my master the sovereign is, whether in death or in life, there also your servant is.” [22] And Dawiḏ said to Ittai, “Go, and pass over.” And Ittai the Gittite and all his men and all the little ones who were with him passed over. [23] And all the country was weeping with a loud voice, and all the people were passing over. And the sovereign himself crossed over <dn>את</dn> the wadi Qiḏron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness. [24] And see, Tsaḏoq also came, and all the Lĕwites with him, bearing <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And they set down <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and Eḇyathar went up, until all the people had finished passing over from the city. [25] And the sovereign said to Tsaḏoq, “Take <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> back to the city. If I find favour in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> shall bring me back and show me both <dn>את</dn> it and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> dwelling place. [26] “But if <dn>He</dn> says thus, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have no delight in you,’</dq> here I am, let <dn>Him</dn> do to me as seems good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [27] And the sovereign said to Tsaḏoq the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Aḥima‛ats your son, and Yehonathan son of Eḇyathar. [28] “See, I am waiting in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.” [29] So Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar took <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> back to Yerushalayim, and they remained there. [30] And Dawiḏ went up by the Ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up. And he had his head covered and went barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went up. [31] And it was reported to Dawiḏ, saying, “Aḥithophel is among the conspirators with Aḇshalom.” And Dawiḏ said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I pray, turn <dn>את</dn> the counsel of Aḥithophel into foolishness!” [32] And it came to be, when Dawiḏ had come to the top of the mountain, where he bowed himself to <dn>Elohim</dn>, that see, Ḥushai the Arkite came to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head. [33] And Dawiḏ said to him, “If you pass on with me, then you shall become a burden to me. [34] “But if you return to the city, and say to Aḇshalom, ‘I am your servant, O sovereign. As I was servant of your father previously, so I am now your servant,’ then you shall defeat <dn>את</dn> the counsel of Aḥithophel for me. [35] “And are not Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the priests with you there? And it shall be that whatever word you hear from the sovereign’s house, you shall report it to Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the priests. [36] “See, they have there with them their two sons, Aḥima‛ats, Tsaḏoq’s son, and Yehonathan, Eḇyathar’s son. And by them you shall send to me whatever word you hear.” [37] So Ḥushai, Dawiḏ’s friend, went into the city. And Aḇshalom came into Yerushalayim.

readings.title: A False Report
readings.subtitle: Ziba and the Provisions
readings.text: [2 Samuel 16:1] And when Dawiḏ had passed on a little from the top of the mountain, see, Tsiḇa the servant of Mephiḇosheth met him, with a couple of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine. [2] And the sovereign said to Tsiḇa, “What are these for?” And Tsiḇa said, “The donkeys are for the sovereign’s household to ride on, and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who are faint in the wilderness to drink.” [3] And the sovereign said, “And where is the son of your master?” And Tsiḇa said to the sovereign, “See, he is staying in Yerushalayim, for he said, ‘Today the house of Yisra’ĕl is going to give back <dn>את</dn> the reign of my father to me.’ ” [4] And the sovereign said to Tsiḇa, “See, all that belongs to Mephiḇosheth is yours.” And Tsiḇa said, “I bow myself, let me find favour in your eyes, my master, O sovereign!”

readings.title: Shim‛i Curses Dawiḏ
readings.subtitle: Slander Along the Road
readings.text: [2 Samuel 16:5] And when Sovereign Dawiḏ came to Baḥurim, see, a man from the clan of the house of Sha’ul, whose name was Shim‛i son of Gĕra, came from there, coming out and cursing as he came. [6] And he threw stones at Dawiḏ and at all the servants of Sovereign Dawiḏ. And all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left. [7] And Shim‛i said thus when he cursed, “Come out! Come out! You man of blood, and man of Beliya‛al! [8] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought upon you all the blood of the house of Sha’ul, in whose place you have reigned. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the reign into the hand of Aḇshalom your son. And see, you are in your own evil, for you are a man of blood!” [9] And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah said to the sovereign, “Why should this dead dog curse my master the sovereign? Please, let me pass over and take off <dn>את</dn> his head!” [10] But the sovereign said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Tseruyah? For let him curse, even because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to him, <dq>‘Curse Dawiḏ.’</dq> Who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’ ” [11] And Dawiḏ said to Aḇishai and all his servants, “See, my son who came from my own body seeks <dn>את</dn> my life. How much more now, this Binyaminite? Leave him alone, and let him curse, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken to him. [12] “If so be, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does look on my affliction, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall return good to me for his cursing today.” [13] And Dawiḏ and his men went in the way, and Shim‛i went along on the hillside parallel to him and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him and kicked up dust. [14] And the sovereign and all the people who were with him became weary, and they refreshed themselves there.

readings.title: The Counsel of Aḥithophel
readings.subtitle: A Bitter Defection
readings.text: [2 Samuel 16:15] And Aḇshalom and all the people, the men of Yisra’ĕl, came to Yerushalayim, and Aḥithophel was with him. [16] And it came to be, when Ḥushai the Arkite, Dawiḏ’s friend, came to Aḇshalom, that Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “Let the sovereign live! Let the sovereign live!” [17] And Aḇshalom said to Ḥushai, “Is this your loving-commitment to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?” [18] And Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “No, but whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and this people and all the men of Yisra’ĕl have chosen, his I am, and with him I remain. [19] “And besides, whom should I serve? Should it not be before his son? As I have served before your father, so I am before you.” [20] And Aḇshalom said to Aḥithophel, “Give your counsel. What should we do?” [21] And Aḥithophel said to Aḇshalom, “Go in to your father’s concubines, whom he has left to guard the house. And all Yisra’ĕl shall hear that you are loathed by your father, and the hands of all who are with you shall be strong.” [22] So they pitched a tent for Aḇshalom on the top of the house, and Aḇshalom went in to his father’s concubines before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl. [23] And the counsel of Aḥithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if one had inquired at the word of <dn>Elohim</dn>. So was all the counsel of Aḥithophel both to Dawiḏ and to Aḇshalom. [2 Samuel 17:1] And Aḥithophel said to Aḇshalom, “Please, let me choose twelve thousand men, and let me arise and pursue Dawiḏ tonight, [2] and come upon him while he is weary and weak, and make him afraid. And all the people who are with him shall flee, and I shall smite <dn>את</dn> the sovereign alone, [3] and bring back all the people to you. When all return except the man whom you seek, all the people shall be at peace.” [4] And the saying was right in the eyes of Aḇshalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Counsel of Ḥushai
readings.subtitle: Buying Time for the Sovereign
readings.text: [2 Samuel 17:5] But Aḇshalom said, “Please call Ḥushai the Arkite also, and let us hear what he, too, says.” [6] And Ḥushai came to Aḇshalom, and Aḇshalom spoke to him, saying, “Aḥithophel has spoken according to this word. Do we do as he says? If not, you speak.” [7] And Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “The counsel that Aḥithophel has given is not good at this time.” [8] And Ḥushai said, “You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are bitter of being, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. And your father is a man of battle, and would not spend the night with the people. [9] “See, he is now hidden in some pit, or in some other place. And it shall be, when some of them fall at the first, that whoever hears it shall say, ‘There is a slaughter among the people who are following Aḇshalom.’ [10] “And even he who is brave, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt. For all Yisra’ĕl knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are brave men. [11] “Therefore I advise that all Yisra’ĕl be completely gathered to you, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa, like the sand that is by the sea for multitude, and that you go to battle in person. [12] “And we shall come upon him in some place where he may be found, and we shall fall on him as the dew falls on the ground. And of him and all the men who are with him there shall not be left even one. [13] “And if he withdraws into a city, then all Yisra’ĕl shall bring ropes to that city, and we shall pull <dn>את</dn> it into the river, until there is not one small stone found there.” [14] And Aḇshalom and all the men of Yisra’ĕl said, “The counsel of Ḥushai the Arkite is better than the counsel of Aḥithophel.” For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had ordained to defeat <dn>את</dn> the good counsel of Aḥithophel, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> might bring <dn>את</dn> evil upon Aḇshalom.
